_note: Commodore 64 Phantasie II art (v1.2; the p2-c64 import, P2C64Art; reverse-engineering/c64/phantasie2/GRAPHICS.md). C64 I's engine: FONT+HER, HSPRIT and the item pictures are I's byte for byte. Monsters are the MX n sprite bands of side 1 (one figure: the band's first sprites, expanded as the VIC does); portraits the HSPRIT pair of each race (none for UNDEAD); the title PIC.* (multicolour bitmap, doubled pixels); town.backdrop the town screen's six buildings at their places (FONT+HER's town characters); the map from II's FONT characters as II's UTIL-3.O routine prints them. Colours: Colodore (VICE colodore.vpl). Text: the remaster 5x7 font (the C64's sets are in font/). The item / feature pictures (items/, I's files and rule) in the programs' colours, beside the find / trap / stairs / lock / exit texts (event.*, find_pictures; DOOR not shown). s221: the ending (WIN's hall from PH2.END-4, TLUM1's crowd; ending_scene) and the party wipe (CEMETARY2's temple, ghost and face through the ST's defeat scene: ui.decor, decor.demon-face, portrait.ghost) in ending/ and defeat/.
name: Commodore 64
_tile_maps: UTIL-3.O $C5C3 (SYS 49152 + 63): map byte b >= 120 prints a blank in black (fog); else class b / 10 prints PETSCII $C697[class] OR (text column AND 1) in colour $C68A[class], one 8 x 8 character a cell, the region's 26 x 20 cells whole (text columns 1-26, rows 5-24): tile b is the even map column's character, b + 256 the odd one's. Bytes 40, 41 and 50 (only 50: I's routine takes 50-59) also place a yellow sprite (town 93, inn 94, dungeon 95) 4 pixels left of the cell (overlays, drawn at their size); the party is white sprite 92 the same way. The Client's map box holds 19 x 18 of the cells around the party (the C64 shows all 26 x 20). Dungeon: as I's, FONT characters $E6-$EC in grey (12) on black by DOS's cell ranges; a cell not yet seen is the solid $20; the party is yellow sprite 91 over its cell.

title_sequence._note: B (v1.2): a credits text screen first (lines 590-670, at least 5 s; not drawn here), then the title picture (PIC.*, lines 185-290) stays up while UTIL-3.O and the two fonts load (no key wait; its time is the disk's [?]), then the '1 - Start in Pippacott / 2 - Continue saved game' text screen. Shown until a key, as the Apple packs do.

_find_pictures: s221 [C] (I's GRAPHICS.md 7, the compiled BASIC of OUTDOORS / DUNGEON, II's the same): a found item shows I$((IT - 1) / 20) (SHIELD ... GOOD TREASURE) in colour IC = 15, 7 if IX = 2 or IX >= 6, 14 if IX = 3, 3 if IX = 4; IX is a float, so the single-id colours hit ids 41, 61 and 81 only. find_pictures: [first id, last id, picture]. event.trap (light red 10, a spotted trap), event.stairs (grey 12), event.lock (brown 9, a locked door, kind 14, whatever the pick), event.exit (green 5, 8 x 6). DOOR is loaded by no program (no slot). The C64 prints them over the map; the Client draws each beside its text.
_portraits: portrait.{race}: HSPRIT (I's file) blocks 2 race (idle) and 2 race + 1 (attacking), the pair the fight copies for a member of that race (C64 I, live s218); yellow, the combat row's colour [~]. No UNDEAD pair.

ending_scene._note: s221 / s223 (GRAPHICS.md 8.1, WIN's compiled BASIC, live in VICE): the intro page, black on yellow, no key: up while PH2.END-4 and TLUM1 load (16.85 s measured with VICE's true drive, PAL [~]); the hall (PH2.END-4) with its cyan panel (the panel's text cyan on inverted characters: black letters); the crowd (TLUM1: 7 expanded green sprites at screen y 110); the whole party in the row from the start (hero band at screen y 75, x 86 + 24 k, yellow); per member: FOR 4000 (4.17 s), the member in light red in its attacking pose in its place while the panel names it (1.09 s) and FOR 4000 (4.17 s), then the cheer: the crowd's second frame for the sound (9.92 s), then the first again (whole cheer 10.22 s). s224: drawn by c64_win (WIN's own steps; the remaster's ending screen fields here are its fallback, unused with c64_win). The closing page black on yellow cells (the hall's inverted characters still loaded). No fade on the C64. s226: the cheer is sid_sounds (I's GRAPHICS.md 9.6).

c64_win._note: s224 (GRAPHICS.md 8.1, WIN's compiled BASIC, timed in VICE PAL with the true drive [~]): the intro page, no key, while PH2.END-4 loads (intro_seconds); the hall alone for FOR 2000 (1.74 s) and TLUM1's load (7.75 s) (hall_seconds); the crowd (frame 0) and the whole party with the header lines (FILMON SPEAKS - at column 2, row 20; the next PRINT at column 0, row 21); FOR 4000 (for_seconds); a cheer; per presented member: FOR 4000; the member light red in its attacking pose with name / THE x ONE / FROM y on rows 20-22 at INT(20 - LEN / 2); FOR 1000 (title_seconds, the prints included); FOR 4000; a cheer; the member yellow again. A cheer: the panel cleared and THE CROWD GOES WILD! (column 10, row 21); the crowd's pointers + 8 at cheer_frame_at for the SID cheer (cheer_frame_seconds), - 8, the panel cleared (cheer_line_seconds), the next step at cheer_seconds. Only WIN's POKEs change the crowd's frame (VICE s224: no interrupt alternates it). The wands prompt (FILMON SPEAKS - at column 2, row 20, the three wand lines from column 0, rows 21-23, then (PRESS RET)) and the closing page each until a key. Core presents the members it titles (records 0..n-1, n = OK members, the ST's rule); the C64 presents every slot [~].

c64_defeat._note: s223 (I's GRAPHICS.md 9.2 / 9.4, CEMETARY's compiled BASIC): runs by itself, no key. 'Your party has been defeated' (red, column 6, row 23), TL = 2; the temple (dark grey) with its door (sprite 7, light grey, x- and y-expanded, behind the characters) and the astral line (blue, column 1, row 23); a ghost per member at VIC y 170, x = INT((220 - 35 PO) / 2) + 35 k, one each TL = 0.3; a sound, TL = 2; the door rises from VIC y 77 to 0, one pixel each TL = 0.1; the face (purple, expanded, in front) and the demon's line, TL = 4; per member the rows cleared (an UNDEAD fate's name on row 21, column 1, cyan: undead_name_row), a sound with TL = 1.08, its line in the fate's colour, its ghost's block overwritten with CSPRIT block P(145) (its own figure) a byte per BASIC pass, still white (64 passes, the 4.1 s copy; s224 morph), then coloured, a destroyed member's then switched off (ON DF GOSUB), TL = 2; TL = 6. The interpreter's time around the waits measured in VICE (PAL, s223) [~]: ghosts 0.33 s apart, the fate sound 1.17 s, the copy 4.1 s. The C64's own fate rule and texts are not used: Core's fates and lines (I's UNDEAD line holds the name too [~]).

sid_sounds._note: s226 (GRAPHICS.md 9.6) [C]: the end screens' sounds as their programs write the SID ($D400 + register), in order; times in seconds from the sound's start (BASIC's TI waits; the VICE-measured interpreter time for the FOR loops, PAL). Played on one 6581 model per screen (Client Sid6581). wind / wind_stop: ZALL $4D40 / $4E46 (P.END step 3 to after the wipe's TD = 2), the IRQ routine $4D73 once a jiffy (zall_wind). thunder: P.END 0xbb6 per strike (its clear loop pokes $D400 only). click / click_off: P.END 0xc43 per space and line end, the gate off after the caller's 16 or RND * 8 jiffies. rumble: CEMETARY 0x90e after the ghosts, its gate never turned off (it sounds until the first fate's clear). fate: CEMETARY 0x97b per member. cheer: WIN 0x749; the sweeps' pass is the measured 9.928 s less the FOR loops at WIN's 1.042 ms a pass [~]. s228 (GRAPHICS.md 9.8) [C]: fight.{outdoors,dungeon}.* = the fights' SID routines of OUTDOORS2 / DUNGEON2 (cast, monster_cast, awakens, alive, miss, hit, encounter, wound, monster_hit, dies, mark), the statements and FOR passes at the times VICE measured (II's routines forced on its fight screen); the TI waits as written. marks: MN field 13 (C%) of monsters 0-79, the marks (each a mark sound) a damage spell draws on that monster. s229: key_click.{town,outdoors,dungeon}: TOWNR 0x510d / OUTDOORS 0x6198 / DUNGEON 0x6a1a (II the same), the input routines' click on each key GET and stick move.
